resources.string: Search by part name, part number, or vehicle model…
Sale saved offline. It posts when the connection is back.
This sale was started online. Finish it when the connection is back, or remove its lines to sell offline.
Offline sales are walk-in only. Customer accounts need the connection.
Discounts, voids, refunds and price changes need a manager online.
Offline selling is not set up on this device.
Not enough stock of %1$s in the last offline snapshot.
OFFLINE SALE · invoice no. issued on sync
Download the whole parts catalogue (about 7 GB: every vehicle, diagram and image) so search, the vehicle picker and EPC work with no connection.
Downloading: %1$s of %2$s (%3$d%%). You can keep selling.
Ready: release %1$s (%2$s), downloaded %3$s. Prices and stock come from the offline sales snapshot.
A staff phone scans parts into the open sale with its own camera.
On a phone signed in with your staff account, open POS → Settings → Scan for a till and enter this code.
Phone connected. Its scans go straight into this sale.
This code has expired. Pair again for a new one.
This part of the catalogue is still being published. Try again later.
The full catalogue is not connected yet (catalogue storage keys are missing).
The parts catalogue is unavailable right now.
%1$s is out of stock. It can be sold once stock is received.
Not enough stock to complete this sale. Reduce or remove the line that is out of stock.
Use this device as the scanner for a till\'s open sale.
Signed in with the same staff account as the till, enter the code the till shows under Pair phone.
Connected. Scans go into the till\'s sale.
Keep your GTR at its best.
No best sellers yet. Long-press any part, category or vehicle to pin it here.
Search by part name, OEM number, PNC or vehicle, or choose a vehicle above.
Search, scan, choose a Popular Item or browse EPC to add parts.
%1$s is being rebuilt on the benchmark design. It is available on the web POS meanwhile.
Best seller removed from Popular Items.
Could not reach the shop server. Check the connection and try again.
This part has no shop price yet. Ask a manager to price it.
Payment status unknown. Check before retrying.
%1$s%% off every non-core line on this sale.
New unit price %1$s for the selected line.
All lines on this sale will be voided.
Name, business, phone, email or customer ID
Nothing to show at this level of the catalogue.
%1$d callouts. Tap one to find its part.
Match the reference numbers on the diagram to the Ref in the parts list.
Diagram image not available. The parts list still works.
Choose a model to browse the parts catalogue
Finish or park the current sale before resuming another.
No vehicles saved for this customer yet.
Short vibrations confirm adds, quantity changes, long-presses and errors.
Discounts, price overrides and voids need a reason. A manager signs in when the approval policy asks for one.
The manager signs in for this action only. You stay signed in.
80 mm receipts print on the counter ESC/POS printer; A4 goes to the document printer.
Refunds need manager approval and post a credit note against the invoice.
USB and Bluetooth scanners type into search. The scan button uses the camera or the paired companion phone.
Management features open after you sign in again.
Walk-in customer. Search or add a customer to attach them to this sale.
Which vehicle is this sale for?
Sale parked. Resume it from Orders.
Customer saved and attached to this sale.
Vehicle saved to the customer\'s garage.
EcoCash request sent to the customer\'s phone.
Payments must add up to the amount due exactly.
Finish or park the current sale first.
Count the float into the drawer. Selling starts once the till is open.
Cash out and handover need a manager to sign in.
Finish or park the current sale before closing the till.
No reasons are set up for this action.
Choose why the drawer is out, then ask a manager to approve the close.
Who is taking over this till? A manager approves the handover.
No other staff can take this till.
Cash leaving the drawer needs a manager to sign in.
Count the drawer by note and coin. The expected total is shown after you submit.
The count does not match. Choose a reason to submit it.
Till open. You can start selling.
Count submitted. A manager must approve the variance.
Open the till before starting a sale.
Within your limit: no manager needed. The reason is recorded in the audit trail.
When discounts, overrides, voids, refunds and cash out need a manager, and whether a reason is required. Only an admin can save changes.
Cash leaving the drawer and till variances always need a manager.
Only an admin can change approval policies.
Approver: hold your ID badge up to the front camera
The front camera opens for an approver\'s ID badge (any manager, or staff with the approval role) once a reason is chosen.
You are signed in as an approver: this is approved under your name.
The camera is not available. Allow camera access, or use the approver password.
This sale is reserved for payment. Go back to the sale to change it.
Reserved checkout is not available on this device.
Waiting for %1$s. The customer approves on their phone.
The customer can scan this code to pay on their phone.
Declined: %1$s. Choose another way to pay.
Declined by the provider. Choose another way to pay.
The customer cancelled. Choose another way to pay.
That payment did not go through and nothing was charged. Try again or choose another way.
This payment could not be confirmed. Do not take money again: resolve it first.
Money was received but the sale did not finish. Do not charge again: an approver finishes it.
The account\'s credit limit, hold and currency are checked when you charge it.
Choose a registered customer to sell on account.
The stock hold expired. Open payment again to reserve it.
Reservation released; the stock is back on sale.
Post the sale for order %1$s against the money already received. Your approval is recorded.
This sale is complete; nothing to resolve.
The provider has not answered yet. Check again before doing anything else.
No money was taken. Release the reservation to put the stock back on sale.

Take the %1$s in parts, for example some cash now and the rest by card. Each part is recorded as it is taken and the sale posts when the parts cover it. If the customer cannot pay the rest, you can finish with only the items already paid for.
Choose the customer first: store credit is theirs.
Not for part payments yet: take it as the whole payment.
The stock goes back on sale. %1$s already received is refunded only after a manager approves it.
The stock goes back on sale. No money has been taken.
Keep only what is paid for
%1$s has been received. Choose what the customer takes; the new total is worked out by the server and cannot be more than that. Anything received over it is refunded.
The customer agreed to take only these items.
Paid in full, but the sale did not post. Do not take more money: resolve it first.
Nothing has been received yet, so there is no paid basket to keep.
Refund reference (cash slip, transfer or reversal number)
A manager or finance approves this with their ID badge, password, or as the signed-in approver.
Part payments cancelled. The sale can be edited or paid again.
Part-paid sale cancelled. The money taken waits for a manager to refund it in Payments to resolve.
Money received over the new total is owed back to the customer. A manager approves the refund in Payments to resolve.
Refund of %1$s from a part payment. Your approval is recorded.
Choose this tablet\'s card machine in Settings.
The card machine app is not installed on this tablet.
An admin must pair this tablet with the card machine (Settings).
No card machine is set up for this shop yet.
Pairing lets %1$s\'s answers be trusted: this tablet signs every result with its own key. An admin signs in for this once (leave blank if you are an admin).
The customer pays on %1$s: insert, tap or swipe the card and enter the PIN on the machine. Card details never come to this tablet.
The customer pays on the machine. The sale finishes on its own when the machine answers. Do not take another payment meanwhile.
The card machine\'s answer did not arrive. Do not charge again: check on the machine first.
The card was charged but the sale did not post. Do not charge again: finish it or reverse it from Payments to resolve.
The card was charged but the sale did not post: %1$s
Give the money back on the machine
This tablet is paired with the card machine.
Reversed on the card machine: the customer was not charged.
Card payment applied: the sale is posted.
Return posted. Pay the customer from the till.
Return posted. Hand over the replacement part.
Return posted and a warranty claim opened. Decide it under Warranty claims.
Core taken back and its charge given back.
Warranty claim opened. A manager decides it under Warranty claims.
Needs a named customer on the sale.
Nothing was paid on this sale.
Part of this sale was already returned: return the rest line by line.
The card machine did not give the money back (%1$s).
Give %1$s back on the card machine for %2$s. The customer uses the same card.
The card machine gave %1$s back. Post the refund.
Open the sale the customer brings back. Only what is still returnable can come back.
For sales paid in full on a card machine, before anything was returned.
Give the money back on %1$s. The customer uses the same card.
The final value comes from the sale, discounts included.
Paid from this till. Only up to what the customer paid.
Lowers what the customer owes. Named customer only.
Credit the customer spends on a later sale. Named customer only.
The returned part goes to quarantine and the same part is handed over.
Opens a warranty claim for one part. A manager decides it later.
Drafted and waiting for an approver. Posting again uses the same return.
The customer brings back the old unit and gets the core charge back.
%1$s · %2$s per core · %3$s of %4$s still due back
Serial number (if the part has one)
That serial belongs to a different part.
Faulty part to quarantine, same part handed over.
Credited at the price it was sold for. Named customer only.
Faulty part goes to quarantine; nothing is credited.
The customer keeps the part. Give the reason.
Held for collection. It becomes ready when the sale is paid.
Held at the other branch. The customer collects it there once the sale is paid.
Transfer requested. Warehouse staff send it.
Transfer sent to the warehouse. It is ready here when the transfer is posted.
Start a sale with this part first.
Add the part to the sale first, so the hold is paid with it.
Kept for 2 hours; ready as soon as the sale is paid.
Order it in; mark it ready when it arrives.
There is stock here: sell or hold it instead.
Nothing held, in transfer or on order. Use Stock by branch on a part card.
Arrived: sell it on a sale, then release this request.
Signature saved. New letters use it.
Add your signature in Settings → My signature first.
A signed record of this payment\'s status for the customer or the bank. Issued by a manager under their own signature.
e.g. Customer asked for proof for their bank
Only a signed-in manager, finance or admin can issue a letter.
This letter records the status of the payment below as seen in our records at the time it was issued. It is not a receipt; a posted sale has its own invoice.
For managers, finance and admins with an employee profile.
On file. Draw below to replace it; letters already issued keep theirs.
No signature on file yet. Payment letters need one.
Sign in the box with a finger or stylus.
Printed at the top of payment letters. Only an admin can save changes.
